name: XDKNet 2.5.4
body:
Android TV 2.5.4, alongside XDKNet server plugin 2.1.0.4 (Emby 2.0.5.4).

TVs on 2.4.10 or later offer this update on their own. On 2.4.9, use
Settings > About > Check for updates. Anything older has to install it once
by hand, from the `XDKNet_AndroidTV.apk` below.

## Why a video is transcoding

The player's stream info and a title's "Direct play: No" list now say why
the server is converting a video. On Jellyfin these were always empty,
because the reasons were read from a place the server never fills. Every
reason Jellyfin and Emby send now has a plain one-line description.

## Safer Seerr setup

The app no longer downloads your Radarr and Sonarr API keys from Seerr. It
only needed to know whether those servers exist, and now asks Seerr in a way
that returns no keys. The plugin also hides API keys and other secrets in
Seerr settings it passes along.

## Server administration (web app)

- **Sessions** counts what is playing, not every connected app, and says how
  many are transcoding and how many are idle. It updates on its own every
  15 seconds.
- **Errors and Warnings** cover the last 24 hours instead of the last 10 log
  lines, and open the Activity page.
- **Disk** now includes your media drives and says how much space is free.
- **Needs Attention** names the plugins with updates and the tasks that
  failed, shows broken plugins and a pending server restart, colours an
  available update as information rather than an error, and no longer
  disappears when one server check fails. Updates that need a newer server
  are no longer offered there or on the Plugins page.
- **Remux, audio converted or transcoding:** sessions, Now Streaming and the
  watch history now tell these apart. A remux only repackages the file, so
  it no longer counts as a transcode.
- **Session details** show the real hardware encoder, and the button that
  only sent the viewer to their home screen now says so.
- **Alerts:** "Failed tasks" and "Server errors" now actually arrive. The
  "Transcode throttling" switch is gone, because nothing could detect it.

The web app gets these with plugin 2.1.0.4 (Emby 2.0.5.4), which carries the
updated web client.

Pair with plugin 2.1.0.4 (Emby 2.0.5.4).
